proofs.proof_tex:
Construct the mixed law as follows.  Let \(X\sim {\rm Unif}[0,1]\), let \(\zeta\) have the centered logistic distribution and be independent of \(X\), and, conditionally on \(X=x\), draw \(A\) as a Bernoulli variable with success probability
\[
\pi _1(x)=\frac{x^{3/2}}2,\qquad \pi _0(x)=1-\frac{x^{3/2}}2 .
\]
Set \(Y(a)=a+X+\zeta\) and \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).  The last equality is \(\text{ass:consistency}\), and the conditional construction of \(A\), together with independence of \(\zeta\), gives \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X\), as required by \(\text{ass:unconfoundedness}\).  Both propensities lie strictly between zero and one except possibly at the two \(P_X\)-null endpoints, so \(\text{ass:positivity}\) holds.

For \(0<t<1/2\),
\[
F_1^\pi(t)
=P\!\left\{X\le (2t)^{2/3}\right\}
=2^{2/3}t^{2/3}.
\]
Thus \(c_1=2^{2/3}\), \(\gamma _1-1=2/3\), and \(\gamma _1=5/3\); the Hall remainder is identically zero.  On the other hand, \(\pi _0(X)\ge1/2\) almost surely, so the stated convention gives \(\gamma _0=\infty\) and \(E\{1/\pi _0(X)\}\le2\).  With \(d_1(x)=x\), \(g_1(x)=-\log2\), and
\[
g_0(x)=\log\!\left(1-\frac{x^{3/2}}2\right),
\]
\(\text{ass:boundary-link}\) holds.  Both \(g_1\) and \(g_0\) belong to a common \(C^{3/2}\) ball.  On a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(d_1=0\), \(\pi _1\le1/2\), which verifies \(\text{ass:opposite-overlap}\).

Write \(\lambda(z)=e^{-z}(1+e^{-z})^{-2}\) and \(\Lambda(z)=(1+e^{-z})^{-1}\).  Then
\[
f_{a\mid X}(y\mid x)=\lambda(y-a-x),\qquad
m_{a,\tau}(x)=\tau-\Lambda\{q_a(\tau)-a-x\}.
\]
The logistic density and its derivative are bounded, so the conditional-density modulus is deterministic and common, and every \(m_{a,\tau}\) is smooth.  Moreover,
\[
f_a(\tau)=\int_0^1\lambda\{q_a(\tau)-a-x\}\,dx>0 .
\]
Because \(\mathcal T\) and \(\mathcal A\) are finite, the minimum of these finitely many positive numbers is positive, proving \(\text{ass:quantile-density}\).  Conditional on \(\pi _1(X)=t\), one has \(X=(2t)^{2/3}\).  The Lipschitz property of \(\Lambda\) therefore gives, uniformly over \(\tau\in\mathcal T\),
\[
\left|\kappa_{1,\tau}(t)-\kappa_{1,\tau}(0)\right|
\le \|\lambda\|_\infty(2t)^{2/3}.
\]
Taking \(G_1\) to be the law of \(1+\zeta\) gives \(\kappa_{1,\tau}(0)=m^{\rm tail}_{1,\tau}\), so \(\text{ass:tail-marks}\) holds with a deterministic power modulus.  The variable \(X+\zeta\) is symmetric about \(1/2\), hence \(q_1(1/2)=3/2\) and
\[
m^{\rm tail}_{1,1/2}
=\frac12-P\{1+\zeta\le3/2\}
=\frac12-\Lambda(1/2)\ne0 .
\]

For a two-heavy family, fix \(s=3/2\) and choose \((\alpha _0,\alpha _1)\) in any compact rectangle contained in \((3/2,\infty)^2\).  Put
\[
\pi _1(x)=\frac{x^{\alpha _1}}
{x^{\alpha _1}+(1-x)^{\alpha _0}},
\qquad
\pi _0(x)=\frac{(1-x)^{\alpha _0}}
{x^{\alpha _1}+(1-x)^{\alpha _0}},
\]
and retain the same outcome construction.  With \(d_1(x)=x\), \(d_0(x)=1-x\), and
\[
g_0(x)=g_1(x)
=-\log\{x^{\alpha _1}+(1-x)^{\alpha _0}\},
\]
the boundary-link and common Hölder conditions hold.  As \(x\downarrow0\),
\[
\pi _1(x)=x^{\alpha _1}\{1+O(x^{\rho})\},
\]
and, as \(x\uparrow1\),
\[
\pi _0(x)=(1-x)^{\alpha _0}\{1+O((1-x)^{\rho})\},
\]
for a common \(\rho>0\) after shrinking the compact parameter rectangle if necessary.  Monotone inversion and \(X\sim{\rm Unif}[0,1]\) give
\[
F_a^\pi(t)=c_at^{1/\alpha _a}\{1+O(t^{\rho_a})\},
\qquad
\gamma _a=1+\frac1{\alpha _a}\in(1,2).
\]
Compactness supplies common positive bounds for \(c_a,\rho_a\) and the validity threshold.  The two zero-propensity endpoints are disjoint, so \(\text{ass:opposite-overlap}\) holds on fixed endpoint neighborhoods.  The preceding logistic calculations supply the common mark and density moduli.  Hence both displayed families are members of \(\mathcal P_{\rm S}\), establishing nonemptiness in the mixed and two-heavy regimes.

Order the finite set as \(\tau_{(1)}<\cdots<\tau_{(R)}\), and abbreviate \(q_r=q_a(\tau_{(r)})\).  Quantile monotonicity gives \(q_1\le\cdots\le q_R\).  Define the cells
\[
C_0=(-\infty,q_1],\quad
C_r=(q_r,q_{r+1}]\ (1\le r<R),\quad
C_R=(q_R,\infty).
\]
Empty cells are allowed.  The vector of threshold indicators, and hence \(\Psi_a(y)\), is constant on every \(C_r\); therefore its support has at most \(R+1\) points.

Put
\[
p_r(t)=K_a(t,(-\infty,q_r]),\qquad
p_r(0)=G_a((-\infty,q_r]).
\]
By the definitions of \(\kappa_{a,\tau}\) and \(\psi_{a,\tau}\),
\[
\kappa_{a,\tau_{(r)}}(t)=\tau_{(r)}-p_r(t),
\qquad
m^{\rm tail}_{a,\tau_{(r)}}=\tau_{(r)}-p_r(0).
\]
Thus \(\text{ass:tail-marks}\) yields
\[
|p_r(t)-p_r(0)|\le\omega_{\rm mark}(t)
\quad(1\le r\le R).
\]
The discrepancies of the cell probabilities are at most
\[
\omega_{\rm mark}(t),\quad
2\omega_{\rm mark}(t),\ldots,2\omega_{\rm mark}(t),\quad
\omega_{\rm mark}(t),
\]
because an interior cell probability is \(p_{r+1}-p_r\).  Total variation on this finite support is one half the sum of the absolute cell discrepancies, and hence
\[
\left\|K_a(t,\cdot)\circ\Psi_a^{-1}-H_a\right\|_{\rm TV}
\le\frac12\{2\omega_{\rm mark}(t)+2(R-1)\omega_{\rm mark}(t)\}
=R\omega_{\rm mark}(t).
\]
The equality with the displayed conditional law follows from the chosen Borel regular conditional kernel \(K_a\).

Finally, if \(\widetilde G_a((-\infty,q_r])=G_a((-\infty,q_r])\) for all \(r\), the preceding cell-difference formulas show that \(\widetilde G_a\) and \(G_a\) assign the same mass to every \(C_r\).  Since \(\Psi_a\) is constant on these cells,
\[
\widetilde G_a\circ\Psi_a^{-1}
=G_a\circ\Psi_a^{-1}
=H_a.
\]
The characteristic exponent in \(\text{def:oracle-limit}\) integrates only with respect to \(H_a\), so it is unchanged by replacing \(G_a\) with \(\widetilde G_a\).

Fix the treated arm of the nonzero-drift mixed witness and abbreviate
\[
\gamma=\gamma_a,\quad h=h_{a,n},\quad
u=\frac{M_n}{h},\quad
\epsilon_n=M_n^{-(\gamma-1)}.
\]
The Hall relation and the generalized-inverse definition imply
\[
c_an h^{-\gamma}\longrightarrow1.
\]
By \(\text{lem:boundary-likelihood}\),
\[
E_{a,n}=o_P(\epsilon_n),
\]
and by \(\text{thm:oracle-preservation}\),
\(\widehat h_{a,n}/h\to_P1\).  On every observation lying strictly inside the fitted tail band, the escape perturbation therefore has relative error
\[
\frac{\widehat\pi^{\rm esc}_{a,-k}}{\pi_a}-1
=(1+\epsilon_n)\left\{1+
\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}-\pi_a}{\pi_a}\right\}-1
=\epsilon_n+o_P(\epsilon_n)
\]
uniformly.  The number of observations with \(\pi_a(X_i)\le u/2\) has mean
\[
nF_a^\pi(u/2)
\sim c_an\left(\frac{M_n}{2h}\right)^{\gamma-1}
\asymp hM_n^{\gamma-1}\longrightarrow\infty .
\]
Its variance is no larger than its mean under \(\text{ass:iid}\), so it is nonzero with probability tending to one.  The upper bound follows from the same display and the \(o_P(\epsilon_n)\) baseline error.  Hence
\[
E^{\rm esc}_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma-1}\to_P1.
\]

For the interior discrepancy, the escape rule differs from the baseline rule on \(\{\pi_a>u\}\) only in a relative-width \(o_P(1)\) shell around \(u\), because \(E_{a,n}=o_P(\epsilon_n)\) and \(\widehat h_{a,n}/h\to_P1\).  Hall integration over that shell, followed by multiplication by \(\epsilon_n\), is \(o_P(1)\).  Since \(D_{a,n}\to_P0\), this proves
\[
D^{\rm esc}_{a,n}\to_P0.
\]
For each fixed \(C<\infty\), \(\epsilon_n\to0\) uniformly on \(h\pi_a\le C\); therefore every fixed-window endpoint mark has the same limit as for the baseline learner.

It remains to compute the mass that escapes through the expanding band.  Let \(S_n^{\rm esc}(\tau)\) and \(S_n(\tau)\) be the normalized linear Knight scores for the perturbed and baseline learners.  Fix \(C>\theta_a\).  Cross-fitting permits conditioning on the training folds.  On \(C/h<\pi_a<M_n/h\), clipping is inactive with probability tending to one and
\[
\frac1{(1+\epsilon_n)\widehat\pi}
-\frac1{\widehat\pi}
=-\frac{\epsilon_n}{1+\epsilon_n}\frac1{\widehat\pi}.
\]
Using the chosen conditional score \(\kappa_{a,\tau}\), the conditional mean of the score difference over this band is
\[
-\frac{\epsilon_n n}{h}\{1+o_P(1)\}
\int_{C/h}^{M_n/h}\kappa_{a,\tau}(t)\,dF_a^\pi(t).
\]
The mark modulus and the Hall expansion give
\[
\int_{C/h}^{M_n/h}\kappa_{a,\tau}(t)\,dF_a^\pi(t)
=m^{\rm tail}_{a,\tau}c_a h^{-(\gamma-1)}
\{M_n^{\gamma-1}-C^{\gamma-1}\}\{1+o(1)\}.
\]
Since \(\epsilon_nM_n^{\gamma-1}=1\), \(c_an h^{-\gamma}\to1\), and
\(\epsilon_nC^{\gamma-1}\to0\), the preceding conditional mean converges to
\[
-m^{\rm tail}_{a,\tau}.
\]
For the centered part, Hall integration yields, for fixed \(C>\theta_a\),
\[
\operatorname{Var}\{S_n^{\rm esc}(\tau)-S_n(\tau)\mid{\rm training}\}
\le
C_1\epsilon_n^2\frac n{h^2}
\int_{C/h}^{M_n/h}t^{-1}\,dF_a^\pi(t)+o_P(1)
=O_P(\epsilon_n^2 C^{\gamma-2})+o_P(1).
\]
This tends to zero because \(1<\gamma<2\).  The clipped region \(h\pi_a\le C\) is a tight fixed-window score multiplied by \(\epsilon_n\), and is therefore \(o_P(1)\); the boundary shell was already shown negligible.  Letting \(C\) be fixed and then large proves, jointly over the finite set \(\mathcal T\),
\[
S_n^{\rm esc}-S_n\to_P-m^{\rm tail}_a .
\]
All empirical drift-correction ingredients are unchanged to first order because the perturbation tends uniformly to one on each fixed window.  The positive-curvature Knight argmin map from \(\text{thm:oracle-preservation}\) therefore gives
\[
\frac n{h_{a,n}}
\{\widehat q^{\,{\rm bc,esc}}_a(\tau)
-\widehat q^{\,{\rm bc}}_a(\tau)\}
\to_P-\frac{m^{\rm tail}_{a,\tau}}{f_a(\tau)} .
\]
The endpoint score is nonzero on the mixed witness by
\(\text{prop:smooth-inclusion}\).  Thus an error of exact order
\(M_n^{-(\gamma_a-1)}\) changes the normalized limit, proving that the amplification order is intrinsic.

The definition of \(\widehat\Delta^{\rm bc}\) gives the exact identity
\[
\frac n{H_n}(\widehat\Delta^{\rm bc}-\Delta)
=\ell_{1,n}\frac n{H_{1,n}}
\{\widehat q_1^{\rm bc}-q_1\}
-\ell_{0,n}\frac n{H_{0,n}}
\{\widehat q_0^{\rm bc}-q_0\}.
\]
The armwise limits are supplied by \(\text{thm:oracle-preservation}\) and the narrowed \(\text{thm:gaussian-branch}\).  Since there are only two arms, their remainder terms are jointly \(o_P(1)\).  Along a subsequence on which \(\ell_{a,n}\to\ell_a\), multiplication by the deterministic convergent coefficients in the last display yields
\[
\frac n{H_n}(\widehat\Delta^{\rm bc}-\Delta)
\Rightarrow\ell_1L_1-\ell_0L_0.
\]

For a heavy arm, the Hall calculation gives
\[
h_{a,n}=(c_an)^{1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\}.
\]
If \(\gamma_1<\gamma_0<2\), then
\[
\frac{h_{1,n}}{h_{0,n}}
=\frac{c_1^{1/\gamma_1}}{c_0^{1/\gamma_0}}
n^{1/\gamma_1-1/\gamma_0}\{1+o(1)\}
\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
so the smaller index dominates.  If \(\gamma_1=\gamma_0=\gamma\), the ratio tends to
\((c_1/c_0)^{1/\gamma}\), so both coefficients have nonzero limits.  Also
\[
\frac{h_{a,n}}{\sqrt n}
=c_a^{1/\gamma_a}n^{1/\gamma_a-1/2}\{1+o(1)\}
\longrightarrow\infty
\quad(\gamma_a<2),
\]
which proves heavy-over-Gaussian dominance.  If both arms are Gaussian, both normalizations equal \(\sqrt n\), and the joint covariance is the covariance of the two influence-function vectors; the common fitted likelihood contribution is therefore retained rather than discarded.

It remains to justify the asserted independence in the two-heavy oracle-preserved case.  Binary propensity coherence and \(\text{ass:opposite-overlap}\) give disjoint fixed neighborhoods of the two zero-propensity endpoints.  For nonnegative compactly supported test functions \(g_0,g_1\) on the two endpoint charts, independence of observations gives a joint Laplace transform of the form
\[
\left[
1-\frac{\nu_{0,n}(1-e^{-g_0})}{n}
-\frac{\nu_{1,n}(1-e^{-g_1})}{n}
+o(n^{-1})
\right]^n.
\]
The two rare events cannot occur for the same observation, so there is no cross term of order \(n^{-1}\).  The Hall and mark limits make
\(\nu_{a,n}(1-e^{-g_a})\to\nu_a(1-e^{-g_a})\); hence the display converges to
\[
\exp\{-\nu_0(1-e^{-g_0})\}
\exp\{-\nu_1(1-e^{-g_1})\}.
\]
This factorization proves independence of the two endpoint Poisson limits.  The finite-arm oracle-transfer errors are jointly \(o_P(1)\), so the same independence holds for the two oracle-preserved feasible endpoint processes.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix \(b_0>1\).  Suppose that \(\mathcal B_J\) is the normalized local B-spline basis on a quasi-uniform partition and that its degree \(r\) satisfies \(r+1\ge s\) and \(2r+1>\sup_{a\in\mathcal A_{\rm H}}\alpha_a\).  Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\rm S}\), heavy arms, fixed folds, and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), the learner satisfies, up to a fixed power of \(\log n\),
\[
\sup_{d_a(x)\ge n^{-b_0}}
\left|\log\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\log\pi_a(x)\right|
=O_P(\delta_{a,n}),
\]
\[
\left|\int m_{a,\tau}(x)
\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\pi_a(x)}{\pi_a(x)}\,dP_X(x)\right|
=O_P\!\left(J_n^{-s}+n^{-1/2}J_n^{(\alpha_a-1)/2}
+\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a}}n\right),
\]
and the corresponding relative-error square integral is
\[
O_P\!\left(J_n^{-2s}+\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a}}n\right).
\]
For \(J_n=\lfloor n^\xi\rfloor\) with
\[
\frac1{s(\alpha_a+1)}<\xi<\frac1{\alpha_a+1},
\]
there is a deterministic \(M_n\uparrow\infty\) such that
\[
E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1),
\qquad
\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|=o_P(1).
\]
At \(\alpha_a=s=3/2\) and \(J_n=\lfloor n^{3/10}\rfloor\), the log-error order is \(O_P(n^{-1/8}{\rm polylog}\,n)\), the signed-functional order is \(O_P(n^{-17/40}{\rm polylog}\,n)\), and the normalized interior discrepancy is \(O_P(n^{-1/40}{\rm polylog}\,n)\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen statement permits degree-zero or otherwise non-approximating spline dictionaries and any positive cutoff exponent. A degree-zero approximation counterexample disproves its asserted log rate; the proposed degree, knot, and cutoff restrictions are estimator-design restrictions and do not shrink the law class.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
On the mixed center in \(\text{prop:smooth-inclusion}\), use the quasi-uniform growing spline schedule in the narrowed boundary-likelihood claim, with \(J_n\to\infty\) and \(J_n\log n/n\to0\).  Then
\[
\inf_x\pi_0(x)=\frac12,\qquad
t_{0,n}\to\frac12,\qquad
h_{0,n}\to2,
\]
\[
\widehat p_{0,(\lceil\widehat h_{0,n}\rceil)}\to_P\frac12,
\qquad
\widehat b_{0,n}\to_P\frac{\vartheta_0}2<\frac12.
\]
Thus clipping is asymptotically inactive on the control arm, its drift correction is zero with probability tending to one, and its feasible objective equals the untrimmed fitted-weight objective with probability tending to one.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: A fixed one-block schedule is allowed by the frozen construction and its population log-boundary score is nonzero on the mixed control, so the fitted lower order statistics do not recover the essential infimum one half. The growing regular-sieve restriction is therefore necessary, and the drift correction can only be asserted to vanish with probability tending to one after empirical regime classification.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(a\in\mathcal A_{\rm G}\), use a normalized quasi-uniform spline basis of degree sufficient for \(C^s\) approximation and a growing dimension satisfying
\[
J_n\to\infty,\qquad
\sqrt n\,J_n^{-2s}\to0,\qquad
\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a}}{\sqrt n}\to0,\qquad
\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a+1}\log n}{n}\to0,
\]
with \(\alpha_a=0\) under the bounded-support convention.  Then the data-driven clip is asymptotically inactive when the propensity is bounded away from zero and is first-order negligible otherwise under \(\text{ass:finite-variance}\).  The cross-fitted likelihood construction satisfies
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat q_a(\tau)-q_a(\tau)\}
=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n{\rm IF}_a(O_i;\tau)+o_P(1)
\]
jointly over \(a\in\mathcal A_{\rm G}\) and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), with covariance \(E_P[{\rm IF}_a{\rm IF}_{a'}^\top]\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The unrestricted theorem is false for an allowed fixed one-block learner: a smooth bounded propensity perturbation orthogonal to its likelihood scores but not to the outcome score makes the weighted quantile inconsistent. The proposed primitive spline and undersmoothing conditions exclude that counterexample without assuming the desired signed-score expansion.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\) and the armwise learner and tuning hypotheses of \(\text{thm:oracle-preservation}\) and the narrowed \(\text{thm:gaussian-branch}\), along each subsequence with \(\ell_{a,n}\to\ell_a\),
\[
\frac n{H_n}(\widehat\Delta^{\rm bc}-\Delta)
\Rightarrow \ell_1L_1-\ell_0L_0,
\]
where \(L_a=\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}/f_a\) for \(a\in\mathcal A_{\rm H}\), and \(L_a\) is the Gaussian vector generated by \({\rm IF}_a\) for \(a\in\mathcal A_{\rm G}\).  Unequal heavy indices are dominated by the smaller index, equal heavy indices retain both endpoint constants, a heavy arm dominates a finite-variance arm, and two finite-variance arms retain their shared learned-score covariance.  In the oracle-preserved two-heavy regime the endpoint processes are independent because their rare-event endpoint sets are disjoint.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The joint theorem must carry the estimator-side hypotheses of its heavy and Gaussian arm inputs. Without them the explicit intercept-only mixed-law counterexample makes the QTE inconsistent.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\), \(\text{ass:anti-concentration}\), and the regular armwise learner schedules in the narrowed heavy and Gaussian claims imposed both at sample size \(n\) and after every refit at sample size \(m\), where \(m\to\infty\) and \(m/n\to0\), conditionally on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), the law of
\[
(T_{B,n}(\tau))_{\tau\in\mathcal T}
\]
consistently estimates the limit in the narrowed \(\text{thm:joint-qte}\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\rm S}\).  For every \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), the pointwise interval
\[
\left[
\widehat\Delta^{\rm bc}(\tau)-\frac{\widehat H_n}{n}
c_{n,1-\alpha/2}(\tau),\ 
\widehat\Delta^{\rm bc}(\tau)-\frac{\widehat H_n}{n}
c_{n,\alpha/2}(\tau)
\right]
\]
has asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\rm S}\) and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\).  For local unequal-heavy-tail sequences whose index gap has exact order \(1/\log n\), raw scalar QTE subsampling at any fixed polynomial rate strictly between constant and linear generally converges to the wrong arm mixture.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Uniform refitted inference requires the regular learner schedule at both sample sizes. The unrestricted algorithm permits an inconsistent fixed sieve, so its original uniform coverage assertion is false.

Unequal heavy indices are dominated by the smaller index, equal heavy indices retain both endpoint constants, a heavy arm dominates a finite-variance arm, and two finite-variance arms retain their shared learned-score covariance.  In the oracle-preserved two-heavy regime the endpoint processes are independent because their rare-event endpoint sets are disjoint.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Make the estimator-side conditions of the two armwise inputs explicit in the joint claim.

proposed.statement:
Under \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\), \(\text{ass:anti-concentration}\), and the regular armwise learner schedules in the narrowed heavy and Gaussian claims imposed both at sample size \(n\) and after every refit at sample size \(m\), where \(m\to\infty\) and \(m/n\to0\), conditionally on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), the law of
\[
(T_{B,n}(\tau))_{\tau\in\mathcal T}
\]
consistently estimates the limit in the narrowed \(\text{thm:joint-qte}\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\rm S}\).  For every \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), the pointwise interval
\[
\left[
\widehat\Delta^{\rm bc}(\tau)-\frac{\widehat H_n}{n}
c_{n,1-\alpha/2}(\tau),\ 
\widehat\Delta^{\rm bc}(\tau)-\frac{\widehat H_n}{n}
c_{n,\alpha/2}(\tau)
\right]
\]
has asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\rm S}\) and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\).  For local unequal-heavy-tail sequences whose index gap has exact order \(1/\log n\), raw scalar QTE subsampling at any fixed polynomial rate strictly between constant and linear generally converges to the wrong arm mixture.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Record the full-sample and refit schedule restrictions.

open_obligations.what_is_open: After the necessary dictionary narrowing, prove the uniform constrained Bernoulli likelihood expansion with a random Hessian and the signed weighted functional rate.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen assumptions provide smoothness and Hall tails but no established lower bound for every local Fisher block, no control of the constrained maximizer under separation, and no proof that score cancellation survives the singular log-boundary direction.
open_obligations.attempted: Derived the Hall normalization, optimized the three claimed error terms, checked the nonempty dimension window, and tested the approximation floor. The degree-zero test gives an explicit counterexample to the unrestricted claim.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The Hall equation gives
\[
t_{a,n}=(c_an)^{-1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\},
\qquad
h_{a,n}=(c_an)^{1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\},
\qquad
\frac n{h_{a,n}}\asymp n^{1/(\alpha_a+1)}.
\]
Consequently, if the three asserted likelihood bounds are available and \(J_n=n^\xi\), their contributions to the normalized signed discrepancy have respective orders
\[
n^{1/(\alpha_a+1)-s\xi},\qquad
n^{1/(\alpha_a+1)-1/2+\xi(\alpha_a-1)/2},\qquad
n^{1/(\alpha_a+1)-1+\alpha_a\xi}.
\]
All three tend to zero exactly under the displayed sufficient window
\[
\frac1{s(\alpha_a+1)}<\xi<\frac1{\alpha_a+1}.
\]
At \(\alpha_a=s=3/2\) and \(\xi=3/10\), the log rate is \(n^{-1/8}\), the signed rate is \(n^{-17/40}\), and multiplication by \(n/h_{a,n}\asymp n^{2/5}\) gives \(n^{-1/40}\).

The unrestricted frozen claim is nevertheless false.  It permits \(r=0\).  For a degree-zero quasi-uniform spline space and a smooth \(g\) with derivative nonzero on a fixed interior interval, the best uniform approximation error is bounded below by \(cJ^{-1}\).  Choose \(s>(\alpha_a+3)/(\alpha_a+1)\) and
\[
\frac1{s(\alpha_a+1)}<\xi<\frac1{\alpha_a+3}.
\]
Then \(J_n^{-s}+\{J_n^{\alpha_a+1}/n\}^{1/2}=o(J_n^{-1})\), contradicting the asserted log-error rate already at the population approximation level.  This proves the necessity of narrowing the dictionary and degree.  What remains unproved after that narrowing is the constrained random-Hessian expansion producing the signed, rather than absolute, functional rate.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove uniform consistency and tail-regime classification of the actual bounded-arm constrained series fit under the proposed growing schedule.
open_obligations.obstruction: The population generalized inverse is elementary, but the empirical order statistic is a functional of the fitted propensity. No bounded-arm uniform likelihood theorem is presently a frozen or proved dependency.
open_obligations.attempted: Computed the population scale and the population log-boundary likelihood score for a fixed one-block fit. Its positive boundary coefficient supplies a direct counterexample to the original empirical order-statistic limits.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For the mixed law, \(F_0^\pi(t)=0\) for \(t\le1/2\), while \(F_0^\pi(t)>0\) for every \(t>1/2\).  Hence the generalized-inverse definition directly gives
\[
t_{0,n}\downarrow\frac12,\qquad h_{0,n}\to2.
\]
The empirical conclusions do not follow for an arbitrary allowed sieve schedule.  Indeed, take \(J_n\equiv1\), so that the bounded-arm fit contains an intercept and the required coefficient of \(\log(1-x)\).  At coefficient zero, the intercept-only fitted probability is
\[
E\{\pi_0(X)\}
=1-\frac12E(X^{3/2})
=1-\frac15
=\frac45.
\]
The population likelihood derivative in the log-boundary direction at this fit is
\[
\frac1{1-4/5}
E\!\left[\{\pi_0(X)-4/5\}\log(1-X)\right]>0,
\]
because \(\pi_0(X)\) and \(\log(1-X)\) are nonconstant decreasing functions of \(X\), and hence have strictly positive covariance.  Thus the population maximizer has a positive boundary coefficient.  Its fitted propensity approaches zero at the largest sample order statistics, rather than approaching the true lower endpoint \(1/2\).  Consequently the claimed fitted order-statistic limit fails.  A growing, uniformly consistent bounded-arm likelihood fit is therefore a necessary restriction; proving that fit for the actual constrained rule is the remaining step.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Establish uniform consistency of every wholly empirical centering component after the feasible-to-oracle score and curvature transfer.
open_obligations.obstruction: The current primitives do not control the fitted Hill statistic at the intermediate order, the nested preliminary quantiles, the random endpoint-score denominator, or the weighted kernel density uniformly over the class.
open_obligations.attempted: Proved the corrected score-transfer inequality from the amplified tail error and the interior discrepancy, and reduced the Knight curvature to the stated density modulus and relative-square bound.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(S^{\rm fe}_{a,n}(\tau)\) and \(S^{\rm or}_{a,n}(\tau)\) denote the feasible and population-weight linear Knight scores, both divided by \(h_{a,n}\).  On \(\{\pi_a\le u_{a,n}\}\), the reciprocal identity
\[
\frac1{\widehat\pi\vee b}-\frac1{\pi\vee b}
=-\frac{\widehat\pi-\pi}
{(\widehat\pi\vee b)(\pi\vee b)}
\]
and the punctured relative bound imply
\[
|S^{\rm fe}_{a,n}-S^{\rm or}_{a,n}|
\le C E_{a,n}\,h_{a,n}^{-1}
\sum_{i=1}^n
\frac{\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\ \pi_a(X_i)\le u_{a,n}\}}
{\pi_a(X_i)\vee b_{a,n}}
+|D_{a,n}|+o_P(1).
\]
Hall integration gives
\[
E\!\left[
h_{a,n}^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n
\frac{\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\ \pi_a(X_i)\le u_{a,n}\}}
{\pi_a(X_i)\vee b_{a,n}}
\right]
=O(M_n^{\gamma_a-1}),
\]
and its centered part has no larger order after truncation.  Hence
\[
\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}
|S^{\rm fe}_{a,n}(\tau)-S^{\rm or}_{a,n}(\tau)|
=O_P\{E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}\}
+\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|+o_P(1)
=o_P(1).
\]
The conditional-density modulus similarly turns Knight's integral remainder into
\[
\frac12f_a(\tau)t^2+o_P(1)
\]
uniformly for bounded \(t\), once the relative-weight square integral is available.  Thus the score-transfer and curvature portions reduce rigorously to the narrowed boundary-likelihood lemma.  Still missing are uniform consistency proofs for the generalized-inverse scale, the nested preliminary quantiles, the fitted-tail Hill statistic, the endpoint-score ratio, and the weighted density estimate.  None of those conclusions is implied merely by the three likelihood bounds, so the full theorem remains open.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove the finite-inverse-moment signed likelihood-functional expansion for the actual constrained cross-fitted sieve.
open_obligations.obstruction: Finite inverse moments make the oracle score square integrable but do not make the learned propensity contribution negligible. The efficient influence function requires a projection identity that is not a consequence of the heavy-arm likelihood lemma.
open_obligations.attempted: Derived the exact first-order decomposition and the projection term required to obtain the advertised influence function. A smooth bounded-propensity perturbation orthogonal to the fixed likelihood scores disproves the unrestricted theorem.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For any cross-fitted propensity learner for which reciprocal linearization is valid, the quantile score expansion is
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat q_a(\tau)-q_a(\tau)\}
=\frac1{f_a(\tau)}
\left[
\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
\frac{\mathbf1\{A_i=a\}\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)}{\pi_a(X_i)}
-\sqrt n\sum_{k=1}^K\frac{|I_k|}{n}
\int m_{a,\tau}(x)
\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\pi_a(x)}{\pi_a(x)}\,dP_X(x)
\right]+o_P(1).
\]
If the likelihood functional in the second term has expansion
\[
\sqrt n\sum_{k=1}^K\frac{|I_k|}{n}
\int m_{a,\tau}
\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}-\pi_a}{\pi_a}\,dP_X
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
\frac{\{\mathbf1(A_i=a)-\pi_a(X_i)\}m_{a,\tau}(X_i)}
{\pi_a(X_i)}+o_P(1),
\]
then subtraction gives exactly the displayed \({\rm IF}_a\).  This identifies the missing signed-likelihood calculation.

The unrestricted frozen theorem is false.  To see this without relying on boundary behavior, take \(d_0(x)=1-x\), choose a constant \(p_0\in(0,1)\), and let
\[
\pi_0(x)=p_0+\varepsilon v(x),
\]
where \(v\) is smooth,
\[
\int_0^1v(x)\,dx=0,\qquad
\int_0^1v(x)\log(1-x)\,dx=0,
\]
but
\[
\int_0^1v(x)m_{0,1/2}(x)\,dx\ne0.
\]
Such a \(v\) exists because the smooth function
\(m_{0,1/2}(x)=1/2-\Lambda(1/2-x)\) is not in the linear span of \(1\) and \(\log(1-x)\).  Equivalently, among three smooth bumps supported inside \((0,1)\), one can choose a linear combination annihilating the first two displayed linear functionals but not the functional obtained by integration against \(m_{0,1/2}\).  For sufficiently small \(|\varepsilon|\), both arm propensities are bounded away from zero and one and all smooth-class assumptions hold.

With \(J_n\equiv1\), the population likelihood scores for the intercept and the log-boundary coefficient both vanish at the constant fit \(p_0\) by the two displayed orthogonality equations.  Strict concavity makes that constant the population maximizer.  At the marginal median,
\[
E\!\left[
\frac{\mathbf1\{A=0\}\psi_{0,1/2}(Y)}{p_0}
\right]
=\frac{\varepsilon}{p_0}
\int_0^1v(x)m_{0,1/2}(x)\,dx\ne0.
\]
Thus the fixed-sieve weighted quantile is not centered at \(q_0(1/2)\), and the asserted root-\(n\) expansion fails.  A growing regular sieve and its weighted signed-functional expansion are indispensable; that expansion remains open.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove uniform conditional reproduction of the joint arm-vector law after refitting the entire algorithm at sample size m.
open_obligations.obstruction: The model assumptions alone do not supply uniform learner, Hill, scale, drift, density, and conditional empirical-law approximations simultaneously at sample sizes n and m.
open_obligations.attempted: Verified that full-sample centering is negligible on each separated arm scale and constructed a local one-over-log-n unequal-index sequence showing that raw scalar subsampling has the wrong mixture weights.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The centering required by \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) subsampling is negligible at every separated arm regime.  For a heavy arm with index \(\gamma_a\),
\[
\frac m{H_{a,m}}
\{\widehat q_a^{\rm bc}-q_a\}
=O_P\!\left[
\frac m{m^{1/\gamma_a}}\frac{n^{1/\gamma_a}}n
\right]
=O_P\!\left\{(m/n)^{1-1/\gamma_a}\right\}
=o_P(1),
\]
and for a Gaussian arm the corresponding order is
\[
O_P\{\sqrt{m/n}\}=o_P(1).
\]
Thus armwise refitting and centering have the correct deterministic scale, provided the armwise laws are reproduced at sample size \(m\).

The raw-scalar failure can be calculated explicitly.  Let
\[
\gamma_{0,n}=\gamma+\frac{c}{2\log n},
\qquad
\gamma_{1,n}=\gamma-\frac{c}{2\log n},
\qquad 1<\gamma<2,\quad c\ne0,
\]
and keep the Hall constants fixed.  Then
\[
\log\frac{h_{0,n}}{h_{1,n}}
=\left(\frac1{\gamma_{0,n}}-\frac1{\gamma_{1,n}}\right)\log n+O(1)
\longrightarrow-\frac c{\gamma^2}+O(1),
\]
whereas for \(m=n^\beta\),
\[
\log\frac{h_{0,m}}{h_{1,m}}
\longrightarrow-\frac{\beta c}{\gamma^2}+O(1).
\]
For \(0<\beta<1\), these are generally different mixture weights.  Taking two nondegenerate endpoint mark laws makes the resulting scalar mixtures different, proving the last sentence of the narrowed claim.

The full uniform conditional-law assertion remains unproved because the current primitives do not establish, at both \(n\) and \(m\), uniform Hill classification, generalized-inverse scale consistency, endpoint-drift estimation, density estimation, and conditional empirical subsampling approximation.  The intercept-only counterexample in the Gaussian partial result also makes the unrestricted original coverage statement false.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Classify the critical fold-labelled Poisson functional into infinitely divisible, Cox, and genuinely fold-coupled cases using primitive conditions.
open_obligations.obstruction: The handle does not specify the limiting constrained-likelihood map or compensator. Different measurable maps compatible with it produce each of the three requested classes, so no necessary-and-sufficient classification follows from the frozen core.
open_obligations.attempted: Reduced every possible subsequential critical law to a measurable fold-labelled Poisson functional and isolated the shared-training inputs that prevent independent marking.
open_obligations.partial_result:
At critical resolution, let \(N_1,\ldots,N_K\) denote the fold-labelled endpoint Poisson limits.  Any subsequential limit allowed by the handle must have the measurable form
\[
\mathcal S
=\sum_{k=1}^K
\left[
\int \Phi_k\!\left(z,y;\,
\mathcal L_k(N_1,\ldots,N_{k-1},N_{k+1},\ldots,N_K)\right)dN_k(z,y)
-\mathcal C_k(N_1,\ldots,N_K)
\right],
\]
followed by the positive-curvature quantile argmin map.  Here \(\mathcal L_k\) is the limiting constrained-likelihood map trained off fold \(k\), and \(\mathcal C_k\) is its compensator.  This representation follows from foldwise cross-fitting and the definition of \(\mathfrak H_{\rm fold}\).

The frozen primitives do not specify the maps \(\mathcal L_k\), their boundary constraint geometry, or convergence of the compensators.  Because \(\mathcal L_k\) and \(\mathcal L_{k'}\) share Poisson inputs, the marks need not be independently marked.  A deterministic \(\mathcal L_k\) gives an ordinary infinitely divisible Poisson integral; an exogenous random intensity can give a Cox mixture; and a shared fold functional can give a law that is neither.  All three behaviors are compatible with the stated handle.  Therefore no necessary-and-sufficient primitive classification can be derived until the critical constrained-likelihood map and its compensator convergence are specified.
